metadata.title: Shafi‘i fiqh corpus expansion: distinct works and evidenced textual relationships
metadata.scope: Classical and continuing traditional Shafi‘i substantive law, with connected commentary, gloss, fatwa, pilgrimage and public-law branches.
metadata.method: Identity and relationship records are checked against named scholarly reference articles and digitized-book catalogues. This is bibliographical verification, not full-text collation of every book. Dates are author death dates only, never inferred composition dates. Unconfirmed and disputed dates remain null. Editions, alternate titles, co-printed works, compilers and continuations are distinguished.
limitations: Bibliographical reference verification is not full-text collation of every book.
Dates are author death dates, not composition dates. Exact CE years are deliberately absent for disputed, approximate, or partially checked chronology.
No unsupported composition places, pedagogical chains, or general-influence edges are asserted.
Two elementary manuals combine doctrine and practical law and are explicitly labelled in their notes.
Corpus is a substantial connected selection, not an exhaustive bibliography of Shafi‘i fiqh.
metadata.audit: Identity and relation audit with dedicated author/work articles, independent manuscript/publisher catalogues and targeted Jordan Iftaa reference passages. Alternate titles and joint printings remain deduplicated. Author-death dates only; uncertain dates left null.
